input: The nurse records the confirmed diabetes and current oral treatment separately from the unclassified episode and the unmeasured hearing complaint.
The driver has confirmed type 2 diabetes, and the current GP medication reconciliation states that diabetes is treated with oral medication.

The driver takes the prescribed tablets and explicitly denies current insulin use; an old appointment reminder about discussing injectable options is not a prescription and has not been treated as evidence that an injection was started.

After a delayed lunch last month he felt shaky and ate a snack without assistance, but glucose was measured only after the symptoms settled, so the nurse has no verified measurement during that event and no treating-clinician classification of severe hypoglycaemia.
He has brought four weeks of glucose entries rather than a complete three-month record, and the specialist review has not yet occurred.
The ophthalmologist confirms non-physiological diplopia following a recent examination.
Diplopia is present within 20 degrees of central fixation.

The driver says the double image is more noticeable after prolonged night driving, yet the specialist reproduced it during daytime testing, so its absence during a short nursing interview is not treated as proof that the documented finding has resolved.
